Coforma is hiring a Junior Software Engineer to build and support a large-scale travel reimbursement system for a federal government client. The role focuses on writing and testing production code, supporting Microsoft Dynamics 365 and .NET services, and contributing to integrations, production support, and secure software delivery.
Consulting
Healthcare
Health Care
No H1B
Responsibilities
Write, test, and ship well-scoped production code in C#/.NET, with guidance from senior engineers
Write automated tests for your own work, and help grow the team's test coverage
Participate in code review, both receiving feedback and, over time, giving it
Pair with senior engineers on larger features to learn the system's architecture and the reasoning behind it
Help investigate and fix production bugs, learning to read logs, traces, and Application Insights telemetry
Make configuration and customization changes in Microsoft Dynamics 365/Dataverse and Power Platform, with training and support
Write and maintain clear technical documentation as you learn areas of the system
Participate in sprint ceremonies, estimate your own work, and communicate progress and blockers early
Follow secure coding practices appropriate to a system handling PII and payment data, under a federal Authority to Operate

Required
A minimum of one year of professional software engineering experience, **OR** equivalent experience through a degree in computer science or a related field, a coding bootcamp, military service, apprenticeship, open-source contribution, or demonstrated self-taught work
Working proficiency in at least one object-oriented or general-purpose programming language
Java, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, or C++ are all reasonable starting points if you're willing to work primarily in C#
Understanding of core programming fundamentals: data structures, control flow, functions and classes, error handling, and reading someone else's code
Familiarity with SQL and relational database concepts, including tables, keys, joins
Basic understanding of HTTP, REST APIs, and JSON
Experience using Git for version control, including branches and pull requests
Some exposure to automated testing (unit tests at minimum) and a willingness to make it a habit
Clear written and verbal communication with the ability to explain what you did, what you tried, and where you're stuck
Genuine curiosity and persistence: you dig into a problem before asking, and you ask clearly when you're actually blocked
Comfortable asking for help and working on a remote team distributed across multiple time zones
Full-time resident of the contiguous United States (must be legally authorized to work in the US now and in the future without sponsorship)
C# strongly preferred
Experience with C# and .NET specifically
Any exposure to Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Dynamics 365/Dataverse, or the Power Platform
Experience with CI/CD pipelines, GitHub Actions, or Azure DevOps
Exposure to cloud concepts—managed services, environments, deployments, logging
Front-end experience with TypeScript and a modern framework
Awareness of web accessibility (Section 508/WCAG) and secure coding basics
Interest in or prior exposure to federal government or civic technology work
Experience working in an agile team with sprints and code review
